title: The Bitter Lesson
description: Rich Sutton's seminal essay on the historic pattern of AI research — leveraging massive computation beats human-engineered knowledge.

title: Attention Is All You Need
description: The paper that changed everything — introducing the Transformer architecture. Understanding this is the price of admission to modern AI.

title: Lil'Log by Lillian Weng
description: Some of the clearest technical writing on LLMs, reinforcement learning, and diffusion models. A masterclass in distilling complex papers.

title: Distill.pub
description: Scientific visualization and interactive explanation at its finest. The gold standard for making ML research genuinely understandable.

title: The Annotated Transformer
description: The Transformer paper with line-by-line PyTorch implementation. Reading this is how you go from 'I get the idea' to 'I can build it'.

title: Karpathy's Neural Networks: Zero to Hero
description: Andrej Karpathy builds neural nets from absolute scratch — no frameworks, just math and code. The best way to actually understand backpropagation.

title: Gwern.net
description: A sprawling, meticulous library of essays on AI, statistics, and rationality. Gwern's analysis on scaling laws is required reading.

title: Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction
description: The Bible of RL by Sutton & Barto. If you want to build agents that learn from interaction, this book is non-negotiable.

title: The Art of Unix Programming
description: Eric Raymond's deep dive into the philosophy and practice that shaped modern software. Why Unix is the way it is.

title: Systems Performance (Brendan Gregg)
description: The definitive guide to understanding system performance from kernel to application. A reference I keep within arm's reach.

title: Computer Systems: A Programmer's Perspective
description: The book that makes you understand what your code actually does at the hardware level. Linkers, cache hierarchies, virtual memory.

title: MIT 6.824 Distributed Systems
description: The canonical distributed systems course. Lectures, labs, and papers on RPC, consensus, replication, and fault tolerance.

title: Tailscale Blog
description: Deep technical dives on building mesh VPNs, WireGuard internals, and networking at scale. They consistently publish engineering gold.

title: The System Design Primer
description: A comprehensive collection of system design resources. Load balancers, CDNs, consensus algorithms explained with diagrams.

title: Google Site Reliability Engineering Books
description: Google's free SRE books — how the world's largest systems are built, monitored, and maintained. Practical wisdom from the people who run the internet.

title: Teach Yourself Computer Science
description: A self-directed curriculum covering the essential CS topics. No fluff, just the real stuff.

title: MIT Missing Semester
description: The tools every programmer should know but nobody teaches — shell, version control, debugging, metaprogramming, and security.

title: Crafting Interpreters
description: Build a full programming language interpreter from scratch — parsing, bytecode, garbage collection. One of the best technical books ever written.

title: Operating Systems: Three Easy Pieces
description: The modern OS textbook. Virtualization, concurrency, persistence — explained with clarity.

title: Build Your Own X
description: A curated list of projects that teach you how things work by building them from scratch — databases, git, Docker, compilers.

title: NAND to Tetris
description: Build a complete computer system from NAND gates up to Tetris. The most satisfying intellectual journey in computer science.

title: PX4 Autopilot Guide
description: The professional open-source autopilot for drones and UAVs. If you're serious about autonomous flight, this is where you start.

title: ArduPilot Documentation
description: The most versatile open-source autopilot system. Supports everything from quadcopters to submarines to rovers.

title: ROS 2 Documentation
description: The Robot Operating System — actually a middleware framework. The lingua franca of modern robotics development.

title: Embedded Rust Book
description: Rust for bare-metal embedded systems. Memory-safe systems programming for microcontrollers — the future of firmware.

title: 3Blue1Brown
description: The gold standard of mathematical visualization. Grant Sanderson's geometric explanations of linear algebra, calculus, and neural networks are pure art.

title: Better Explained
description: Math lessons that focus on intuition over memorization. Explains e, imaginary numbers, and Bayes' theorem so they actually click.

title: The Feynman Lectures on Physics
description: Feynman's legendary physics lectures, available free online. The gold standard for understanding the fundamental laws of the universe.

title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy
description: Peer-reviewed, deep dives into every major philosophical topic. The closest thing the internet has to a formal philosophical reference library.

title: Inferno Operating System
description: A distributed OS from the creators of UNIX that treats network resources exactly like local files. A glimpse into an alternate computing timeline.

title: The Codeless Code
description: Parables about software engineering inspired by Zen koans. Each story will make you think differently about code, teams, and craftsmanship.

title: Plan 9 from Bell Labs
description: The true successor to Unix — distributed, per-process namespaces, and 9P protocol. It lost the OS war but won the ideas war.

title: Sneakernet Concept
description: A network where data is transferred physically using storage media. Sometimes the highest bandwidth connection is a hard drive on a bicycle.

title: Permacomputing
description: A community of practice around resilience and regenerativity in computing, inspired by permaculture. Challenges infinite growth assumptions.

title: The Cathedral and the Bazaar
description: Eric Raymond's analysis of open source vs closed source development models. The essay that helped define how the internet builds software.

title: Brutalist Websites
description: A gallery of websites that embrace the brutalist web design philosophy — raw, honest, and unpolished by intent.

title: Hacker News
description: Tech's watering hole. Cutting-edge tech discussion, startup news, and the occasional existential crisis.

title: Stratechery by Ben Thompson
description: The sharpest analysis of tech strategy and business models. Thompson's aggregation theory will change how you see the industry.

title: Excalidraw
description: A virtual whiteboard for sketching diagrams. Hand-drawn style, collaborative, and surprisingly powerful for system architecture doodles.

title: Observable
description: Interactive data notebooks in the browser. D3.js meets reactive programming — perfect for exploratory data analysis.

title: Internet Archive
description: The digital time machine — free books, movies, software, and 800 billion web pages. The ultimate bulwark against digital amnesia.

title: OpenWebRX
description: A web-based SDR receiver that lets you listen to the radio spectrum through your browser. Ham radio, weather satellites, maritime beacons worldwide.

title: SICP
description: The legendary CS textbook that teaches programming as a way of thinking. Scheme, metacircular evaluators, and the beauty of abstraction.

title: Code: The Hidden Language of Computer Hardware and Software
description: Charles Petzold's masterful journey from Morse code to CPUs. Explains how computers work at every layer of abstraction.

title: Gödel, Escher, Bach
description: Douglas Hofstadter's Pulitzer-winning exploration of self-reference, formal systems, and consciousness. A book that rewires your brain.

title: The Pragmatic Programmer
description: 20th anniversary edition of the software craftsmanship classic. Knowledge portfolios, DRY, and the broken window theory.

title: Designing Data-Intensive Applications
description: The definitive guide to building reliable, scalable, and maintainable data systems. Non-negotiable if you want to understand distributed systems.

title: The Map of Mathematics
description: A beautiful visual summary of all branches of math — from algebra to topology. Shows how every discipline connects.

title: Explorable Explanations by Nicky Case
description: Interactive simulations that teach complex systems and human behavior. Proves that active interaction beats passive reading.

title: Seeing Theory
description: An interactive guide to probability and statistics from Brown University. Visualizes concepts like Bayes' Theorem intuitively.

title: Snow Leopard Trust
description: The leading organization working to protect snow leopards across Central Asia, including Pakistan's northern regions. Science-based conservation.

title: Markhor — Pakistan's National Animal
description: The magnificent spiral-horned markhor found in Pakistan's northern mountains. A conservation success story — from endangered to vulnerable.

title: Himalayan Brown Bear in Deosai Plains
description: The Deosai National Park in Gilgit-Baltistan protects one of the last remaining habitats of the Himalayan brown bear. A high-altitude wilderness.

title: Hangul Deer — Kashmir's Critically Endangered Red Deer
description: The Hangul (Kashmir stag) is the only surviving subspecies of red deer in South Asia. Found in Dachigam National Park, Kashmir. Critically endangered.

title: Indus River Dolphin
description: One of the world's rarest mammals — the blind Indus river dolphin. Found only in the Indus River system in Pakistan. Fewer than 2,000 remain.

title: Himalayan Monal — National Bird of Nepal
description: The iridescent Himalayan monal (danphe) found across the Himalayas including Azad Kashmir. One of the most visually stunning birds on earth.

title: Musk Deer of Kashmir
description: The elusive Himalayan musk deer, found in the high altitudes of Kashmir and Northern Pakistan. Hunted for its musk gland — critically endangered.

title: Chitral National Park
description: Home to markhor, snow leopards, Tibetan wolves, and the rare western tragopan. One of Pakistan's most biodiverse regions.

title: Kashmir's Dachigam National Park
description: The lifeline of the Hangul deer. Also home to black bears, leopards, and over 150 bird species. A Kashmir valley gem.

title: Astola Island — Pakistan's Offshore Wildlife Haven
description: Pakistan's largest offshore island in the Arabian Sea. Critical nesting site for turtles and seabirds. A forgotten wilderness.

title: Serengeti Live Cam
description: Live streaming wildlife cameras from the Serengeti. Lions, elephants, giraffes, zebras — the greatest wildlife show on earth.

title: ARKive — Wildlife Image Archive (Closed but Mirrored)
description: The world's central repository of wildlife imagery. Now preserved on Internet Archive. Thousands of species photographed and documented.

title: iNaturalist
description: Citizen science platform for identifying and logging wildlife sightings. One of the largest biodiversity databases in the world.

title: WWF Pakistan
description: WWF's Pakistan office working on conservation of the Indus dolphin, snow leopard, markhor, and Pakistan's forests and wetlands.

title: Pakistan Wetlands Program
description: Information on Pakistan's 19 Ramsar wetland sites — critical habitats for migratory birds from Siberia to Africa.

title: Living Desert — Thar & Cholistan Wildlife
description: The surprising biodiversity of Pakistan's desert regions — chinkara gazelle, desert foxes, bustards, and the resilient life of sand dunes.

title: Tibetan Wolf in Pakistan's North
description: The elusive Tibetan wolf found in Pakistan's northern highlands. A key predator in the fragile alpine ecosystem.

title: Vintage Computer Festival
description: The world's largest gathering of vintage computer enthusiasts. See Altairs, PDP-11s, Cray supercomputers, and Apple Is in action.

title: The PDP-11 — The Most Influential Computer Ever?
description: The DEC PDP-11 shaped modern computing more than almost any other machine. UNIX was born on it. C was developed on it.

title: Cray Supercomputers Archive
description: The history of Cray Research — the supercomputers that defined high-performance computing. Vector processors, liquid cooling, and iconic design.

title: RS-6000 — IBM's POWER Architecture Roots
description: The IBM RS/6000 that brought POWER architecture to the world. The machine that ran Deep Blue. The predecessor to modern POWER servers.

title: DEC Alpha — The 64-bit Legend
description: Digital's Alpha architecture — the fastest microprocessor of its era. 64-bit, RISC, and years ahead of its time. The chip that could have taken over the world.

title: SGI Origin — Visual Computing Giants
description: Silicon Graphics workstations and servers — the machines that rendered Jurassic Park and defined 1990s visual computing. MIPS processors, IRIX OS.

title: Sun SPARCstation — The Engineer's Workstation
description: Sun Microsystems' SPARCstation line — the workstation that powered the early internet. SunOS, Solaris, and the rise of RISC.

title: NeXT Computer — The Machine That Built the Web
description: Tim Berners-Lee invented the World Wide Web on a NeXT computer. Steve Jobs' NeXTSTEP became macOS. A machine that changed history.

title: Commodore 64 — The Best-Selling Computer of All Time
description: The Commodore 64 sold 12.5 million units. An entire generation learned to program on this machine. The golden age of home computing.

title: Amiga — The Multimedia Revolution
description: The Commodore Amiga was a decade ahead in graphics, sound, and multitasking. Video Toaster, Deluxe Paint, and a cult that still exists today.

title: ThinkPad History — The Last Great Laptop
description: The IBM/Lenovo ThinkPad lineage. From the iconic 700C to the modern X1. The design language that defined mobile computing for three decades.

title: VAX — The Architecture That Defined Enterprise Computing
description: DEC's VAX architecture dominated enterprise computing for two decades. Virtual memory, VMS, and the machine that ran the world before x86.

title: Toyota Land Cruiser 70 Series — The Indestructible Legend
description: The Land Cruiser 70 Series has been in continuous production since 1984. The definitive off-road vehicle used by NGOs, militaries, and explorers worldwide.

title: Toyota Land Cruiser 100 Series — The Gold Standard
description: The 100 Series Land Cruiser — the vehicle that combines luxury with unmatched off-road capability. IFS, solid rear axle, and the legendary 2UZ-FE V8.

title: Cummins Diesel Engines — The Heart of Heavy Machinery
description: Cummins B-series and ISX diesel engines power everything from pickup trucks to semi-trucks to generators. The 12-valve 5.9L is legendary for reliability.

title: Detroit Diesel 2-Stroke — The Screaming Jimmy
description: The unique 2-stroke Detroit Diesel engines (6-71, 8V-71, 12V-71, 16V-71) — the sound of heavy equipment and highway trucks for decades.

title: Caterpillar D9 — The Bulldozer That Moves Mountains
description: The Caterpillar D9 — a 100,000-pound bulldozer with a 600+ hp diesel engine. Used in mining, construction, and military engineering.

title: Unimog — The Ultimate Off-Road Truck
description: Mercedes-Benz Unimog — a truck that is also a tractor, a crawler, an implement carrier, and a fire engine. Portal axles, extreme articulation, unstoppable.

title: Mitsubishi Pajero/Montero — Dakar Legend
description: The Pajero won the Dakar Rally 12 times. A masterclass in off-road engineering — Super Select 4WD, rugged independent suspension.

title: Nissan Patrol Y61 — The Tough Guy
description: The Nissan Patrol Y61 — solid axles front and rear, the legendary TD42 diesel, and a reputation for being nearly indestructible.

title: The Wärtsilä-Sulzer RTA96-C — The Largest Engine in the World
description: A 109,000-horsepower, 2,300-ton marine diesel engine. 14 cylinders, each with a 38-inch bore. The engine that moves container ships across oceans.

title: Expander — The Overlanding Toyota Coaster Build
description: A custom Toyota Coaster bus converted into a serious overlanding expedition vehicle. The ultimate DIY off-grid mobile workshop.

title: How the Internet Actually Works — DNS Deep Dive
description: An interactive, visual explanation of DNS — from your browser to the root servers to the authoritative name server. The phonebook of the internet.

title: BGP — The Routing Protocol That Holds the Internet Together
description: Border Gateway Protocol (BGP) is how the internet routes traffic between autonomous systems. When BGP breaks, the internet breaks.

title: Internet Exchange Points — The Physical Internet
description: IXPs are the physical locations where ISPs and networks connect to exchange traffic. The real fabric of the internet is in these buildings.

title: Submarine Cable Map
description: An interactive map of the 400+ undersea fiber optic cables that carry 99% of international data traffic. The physical backbone of the internet.

title: How a CPU Works — From Transistors to Computing
description: An interactive visual guide to how a CPU works at the transistor level. ALU, control unit, registers, and the fetch-decode-execute cycle.

title: Starlink — The Satellite Internet Constellation
description: SpaceX's Starlink constellation of thousands of low-earth-orbit satellites providing global internet. The future of rural connectivity and backup infrastructure.

title: Mesh Networking — The Internet Without ISPs
description: How mesh networks like BATMAN, OLSR, and 802.11s allow communities to build their own internet infrastructure without centralized ISPs.

title: Guifi.net — The World's Largest Community Network
description: A massive open, free, and neutral telecommunications network built by citizens in Catalonia. Over 30,000 nodes. Proof that community internet works.

title: NYC Mesh — Community Owned Internet
description: New York City's community mesh network. Installing rooftop antennas and fiber to create an ISP that belongs to its users.

title: AREDN — Amateur Radio Emergency Data Network
description: Amateur radio operators building high-speed data networks using off-the-shelf Wi-Fi gear on ham frequencies. Mesh networking for emergency communications.

title: Meshtastic — Off-Grid Mesh Communication
description: Open-source, off-grid, mesh communication using inexpensive LoRa radios. No cell tower or internet required. Text messaging over miles.

title: Ham Radio General Class Study Guide
description: Complete guide to getting your amateur radio General class license. Unlock HF bands and global communication capability.

title: Winlink — Email Over Radio
description: Global email system that works over ham radio frequencies. No internet required. Used by sailors, remote expeditions, and emergency services.

title: APRS — Automatic Packet Reporting System
description: A digital communication system used by amateur radio operators for real-time tactical communications, position reporting, and messaging.

title: WSJT-X — Weak Signal Digital Modes
description: Software for weak-signal digital communication modes like FT8, JT65, and WSPR. Communicate across the globe with just a few watts.

title: OpenWebRX — Web-Based SDR Receiver
description: Listen to the radio spectrum through your browser. Ham radio operators, weather satellites, and maritime beacons worldwide, right from your laptop.

title: Self-Hosting Guide — Run Your Own Services
description: Comprehensive guide to self-hosting your own services — email, file storage, media streaming, Git, and more. Reclaim your digital sovereignty.

title: YunoHost — Self-Hosting for Everyone
description: A Debian-based distribution that makes self-hosting accessible. One-click install of Nextcloud, Jellyfin, WordPress, and hundreds of apps.

title: Nextcloud — Your Own Cloud Infrastructure
description: Self-hosted productivity platform — files, calendar, contacts, chat, video calls, and collaborative document editing. A true Google Workspace alternative.

title: Jellyfin — Your Own Media Streaming Server
description: Free and open-source media server. Stream your own movies, music, TV shows, and books to any device. No subscriptions. No tracking.

title: Pi-hole — Network-Wide Ad Blocking
description: DNS sinkhole that blocks ads and trackers at the network level. Install on a Raspberry Pi and protect your entire home network.

title: Tor Project — Anonymous Communication
description: The Onion Router — browse the internet anonymously and access the dark web. Critical tool for privacy, circumvention, and free speech.

title: Standard Notes — Encrypted Notes, Self-Hosted
description: End-to-end encrypted notes app with self-hosting option. If you care about your notes being private, this is the answer.

title: CalyxOS — De-Googled Android
description: A privacy-focused Android operating system that removes Google services and tracking. Own your phone again.

title: GrapheneOS — The Most Private Mobile OS
description: Security and privacy hardened Android. Hardened kernel, verified boot, and no Google services by default. The gold standard for mobile privacy.

title: F-Droid — Free and Open Source Android Apps
description: The catalog of FOSS Android applications. No tracking, no ads, no proprietary dependencies. Install apps directly without Google Play.

title: The Pirate Library — Preserving Knowledge
description: A collection of shadow libraries preserving human knowledge. Books, papers, and academic resources that should be accessible to everyone.

title: Sci-Hub — Access to Scientific Knowledge
description: The controversial platform that provides free access to millions of scientific papers behind paywalls. Knowledge should not be locked.

title: Z-Library — The World's Largest Library
description: A shadow library with millions of books and academic articles. One of the largest collections of human knowledge ever assembled.

title: Prepper Tech — Technology for Uncertain Times
description: A comprehensive guide to building technology systems that work when everything else fails. Off-grid power, mesh comms, and local data storage.

title: Off-Grid Solar Power for Tech Infrastructure
description: How to power servers, routers, and communication equipment entirely from solar. Battery sizing, panel selection, and real-world deployments.

title: Survival Communication — When the Internet Goes Dark
description: A practical guide to communication methods that work without internet infrastructure. HAM radio, FRS/GMRS, satellite messengers, and signal mirrors.

title: The Off-Grid Server Stack
description: Building a complete server setup that runs on solar power with satellite internet backup. Own your data regardless of what happens to the grid.

title: Low-Tech Magazine — High-Tech Solutions on a Budget
description: A magazine exploring low-tech, resilient, and sustainable alternatives to high-energy technology. Solar-powered website. No tracking. Pure knowledge.

title: The Prepared — Survival and Resilience
description: A modern, practical guide to preparedness. No bunker mentality — just rational thinking about building resilience into your life and technology.

title: Doomsday Prepper's Guide to Digital Data
description: How to preserve your digital data for decades without cloud services. Optical media, tape backups, redundant storage, and the 3-2-1 rule.

title: Habitat — Sustainable Living and Technology
description: A community exploring how to build resilient, sustainable habitats that integrate technology with ecological principles.

title: The Barter Network — Alternative Economy
description: Community-based barter systems built around mutual credit. As financial systems wobble, understanding alternative economies is a survival skill.

title: Raspberry Pi 5 — The Ultimate Self-Hosting Server
description: The latest Raspberry Pi can run a full personal server stack — Nextcloud, Pi-hole, Jellyfin, and more. All for under $100 and 10 watts.

title: OpenResty — High-Performance Web Server
description: A full-fledged web platform based on Nginx and LuaJIT. Used by Cloudflare, Taobao, and others for high-throughput, low-latency systems.

title: Kubernetes — The Data Center Operating System
description: Kubernetes orchestrates containerized workloads across thousands of machines. The standard for large-scale server deployments.

title: Ceph — Distributed Storage at Petabyte Scale
description: Free and open-source distributed storage system that can handle exabytes of data. Used by CERN, DreamHost, and OVH for massive storage clusters.

title: NixOS — The Reproducible Operating System
description: An OS with declarative configuration and atomic upgrades. Every system state is defined in a config file. Perfect for reproducible server deployments.

title: Proxmox VE — Open Source Data Center Virtualization
description: Enterprise-grade virtualization platform. Run VMs and containers on a single host. The open-source alternative to VMware vSphere.

title: Mainframes — The 99.999% Reliable Computers
description: IBM mainframes like the z16 still power the world's banking, airline, and government systems. Up-time measured in decades, not months.

title: HPC — High Performance Computing Overview
description: An introduction to supercomputing architecture — clusters, interconnects (InfiniBand), parallel file systems, and job scheduling (SLURM).

title: Blade Servers — Density Computing
description: Blade servers pack dozens of server modules into a single chassis sharing power, cooling, and networking. The ultimate in data center density.

title: Data Center Cooling — The Hidden Infrastructure
description: How the world's data centers stay cool. From AC to liquid immersion to building facilities in the Arctic. The invisible cost of cloud computing.

title: Google's Borg — The System That Inspired Kubernetes
description: Google's internal cluster management system that runs billions of containers a week. The paper that inspired Kubernetes and changed infrastructure forever.

title: TempleOS — The Most Interesting OS Ever Written
description: A modern operating system written entirely by one person as a divine creation. 100,000 lines of code, 64-bit, with its own compiler, kernel, and graphics stack.

title: Dwarf Fortress — The Most Complex Simulation in Gaming
description: A simulation game of literally infinite depth. Generates entire worlds with history, geology, ecology, and civilizations. The definition of emergent complexity.

title: Lobsters — The Tech Link Aggregator
description: A community-driven link aggregation site for tech enthusiasts. Less noise than Hacker News, more signal, and actual thoughtful discussion.
